entries.title: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson model and the Brownian web landscape
entries.abstract: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson first passage percolation defines a random directed metric on $\mathbb Z^2$ where the environment is updated according to a Poisson process. We show that its finite dimensional distributions converge after $0:1:2$ scaling to those of the Brownian web landscape defined on the finite dimensional marginals of the dynamical Brownian web. We prove non-uniqueness of geodesics in the Brownian web landscape and we relate it to exact formulas on one-sided reflected Brownian motions. We prove a locally uniform law of large numbers and uniform deviation bounds, and identify Poisson increment-stationary laws for the associated height evolution.

entries.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
entries.abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

entries.title: Particle systems and the supercooled Stefan problem: Long time behaviour and fluctuations
entries.abstract: We consider an infinite system of particles on the positive real line, initiated from a Poisson point process, which move according to Brownian motion up until the hitting time of a barrier. The barrier increases when it is hit, allowing for the possibility of sequences of successive jumps to occur instantaneously. The scaling limit gives a representation for the supercooled Stefan problem and its free boundary, from which we can determine the asymptotic limit for the barrier movement. We establish also a functional central limit theorem describing the fluctuations about this limit, from which we can determine the rate of convergence for particle system approximations to the supercooled Stefan problem under ``weak feedback" assumptions introduced in arXiv:1811.12356. We finally show that these fluctuations are identical to the fluctuations of a continuous analogue to 1D-MDLA.

entries.title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
entries.abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

entries.title: Equivalence of finite and infinite survival and sharpness of the phase transition for additive particle systems
entries.abstract: Krone's two-stage contact process is an interacting particle system in which each site on a grid can be in one of three possible states: 0 (empty), 1 (young individual), and 2 (adult individual). Only adults can multiply, and their offspring is initially young, before growing up after an exponential time. There are two death rates, one for adult trees, and a higher one for young trees. The process is additive and has an additive dual, but unlike the contact process it is not self-dual. Answering a question of Krone, for the process on the $d$-dimensional integer grid, Foxall proved that survival of finite populations is equivalent to nontriviality of the upper invariant law. Using a completely different method, we generalise this result to processes on countable groups and along the way also establish sharpness of the phase transition for a general class of additive interacting particle systems.

entries.title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
entries.abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

entries.title: Critical Branching Systems with General Lifetimes: Hunt Motions and Applications to Semilinear Equations
entries.abstract: We consider a critical monotype Bellman-Harris branching particle system on $E=R^d$ or $E=[0,\infty)^d$, started from a homogeneous Poisson field with Lebesgue intensity. Particles follow a conservative Hunt process with transition semigroup $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$, have independent lifetimes with distribution $Γ$, and reproduce at death with generating function $f(s)=s+c(1-s)^{1+β}$. We assume Lebesgue invariance and uniform bounds $P_t1_K=O(t^{-q})$ for compact $K$. We also impose a localization condition: the expected number of particles in a fixed compact set at time $t$ descended from ancestors initially outside suitable regions of volume $O(t^q)$ can be made arbitrarily small, uniformly for $t\ge 1$. For spread-out lifetimes of finite mean, the system converges to a nontrivial limit of Lebesgue intensity when $qβ>1$ and becomes locally extinct when $qβ\le 1$. For nonarithmetic lifetimes satisfying $\barΓ(t)\sim c_1t^{-γ}$, $0<γ\le 1$, the threshold is $qβ=γ$: the limit is Poisson above it, local extinction holds below it, and a nontrivial subsequential limit exists at equality. We verify the hypotheses and determine recurrence-transience regimes for symmetric and anisotropic stable processes, symmetric uniformly elliptic diffusions, generalized squared-Bessel products on $[0,\infty)^d$, and symmetric bilateral Bessel-type diffusions on $R^d$ and their nonsingular linear images. Finally, we derive quantitative sufficient conditions for survival of total mass in semilinear equations with absorption, including time-dependent diffusion rates. Here survival means that the limiting total mass is strictly positive. For a hyperbolic diffusion, this holds for every $β>0$ in the absorption term $-v^{1+β}$.

entries.title: Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
entries.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.

entries.title: Malliavin structure for conditionally independent random variables
entries.abstract: We consider a countable family of random variables which are conditionally independent given a latent random variable $Z$. Given $Z$, the random variables are independent. Hence the Malliavin calculus for independent random variables applies for each value of $Z$. We show that these constructions fit together. We obtain the chaos decomposition, the domains of the Malliavin operators, the Mehler formula and the carré du champ operator, with conditional expectations given $Z$ in place of ordinary expectations. For normal approximation, conditioning on $Z$ and the infinite de Jong theorem of Döbler give mixed normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. Working under the unconditional probability, we obtain a de Jong type bound for U-statistics whose kernels are products. In both cases, the fluctuations of the conditional variance appear as an additional term, which cannot be removed. As an application, we consider subhypergraph counts in a random $3$-uniform hypergraph built on a latent random graph. For the count centred at its conditional mean, we obtain an explicit rate in Wasserstein distance. It reduces to the known rate for the Erdős--Rényi hypergraph when the latent graph is complete. The count centred at its mean is a pattern count in a non-uniform hypergraph with independent edges, which gives a necessary and sufficient condition for its asymptotic normality.

entries.title: Limit laws for the friendship paradox in random geometric graphs
entries.abstract: The friendship paradox says that, on average, the neighbours of a vertex have more neighbours than the vertex itself. We study the size of this effect, the average over all vertices of the mean degree of the neighbours minus the degree of the vertex, in the random geometric graph on the torus with the maximum-norm distance. We determine its limit law in every regime of the connection radius and quantify the approximation by non-asymptotic error bounds in the Kolmogorov distance or the total variation distance. We also give its exact mean for every $n$ and every radius below one half. For a fixed radius the limit is not Gaussian but a weighted sum of centred exponential variables; when the radius shrinks and the expected degree grows, the statistic is asymptotically Gaussian, with a Berry--Esseen bound; for bounded expected degree it is Gaussian at the classical rate; and when the expected degree tends to zero it is asymptotically Gaussian, Poisson or identically zero, depending on how fast the radius shrinks. When the expected degree is large, the proofs rest on the vanishing of the first Hoeffding projection, which makes a degenerate $U$-statistic of pairs of points the source of the fluctuations; it is analysed by Fourier series for a fixed radius and by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs for a shrinking radius. For bounded expected degree we use normal approximation for local functionals, and for vanishing expected degree the Chen--Stein method.

entries.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
entries.abstract: We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

entries.title: Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels
entries.abstract: We study first-passage percolation on finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel on $N$ vertices. We prove that a uniform absolute spectral gap and an $O(N^{-1})$ bound on a fixed even-step return probability imply the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit and an independent Gaussian hopcount limit. Jointly with these quantities, the entire geodesic from an arbitrary source to an independent uniform target is approximated in total variation by an independent Markov chain stopped at the hopcount. This comparison yields laws of large numbers for fixed-length path segments and joint central limit theorems for bounded additive observables. The results extend to edge laws with a uniform relative hazard error $o(1/\log N)$, including common noise distributions with a power-law hazard and a positive-power error near zero. Applications include integrable singular torus kernels, macroscopic spread-out graphs, non-transitive regular graphs, finite groups, and discretizations of symmetric continuum kernels.

entries.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
entries.abstract: We consider stationary log-correlated random fields of the form \[ X_n(t):= \sum_{j\le n} f(e^{τ_j} t+ v_{j})\,,\quad t\in \mathbb{R} \] for a centered 1-periodic analytic function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, where $(τ_j)_{j\ge1}$ are the arrival times of a rate-1 Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ are iid uniform random variables in $[0,1)$. We show that with high probability, \[ \max_{t\in[-1,1]}X_n(t) = c_1 n + c_2 τ_n- (c_3+o(1))\log n \] where $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are positive constants depending on $f$. In particular, the random frequency $τ_n$ produces a central limit fluctuation of order $\sqrt{n}$, together with a logarithmic correction different from the ubiquitous Bramson correction for models with strong comparisons to Gaussian fields, such as homogeneous branching random walks and log-characteristic polynomials of C$β$E matrices. Our proof makes a connection with branching random walks in random time-environment, where coarse-scale fluctuations of the arrival times $τ_j$ play the role of a quenched random environment, and fine-scale fluctuations are leveraged to establish a branching decorrelation structure. We conjecture analogous asymptotics for the characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices, and expect the same mechanism to arise in other Poissonian fields such as characteristic polynomials of sparse random matrices.

entries.title: Existence of a fluid phase for the two-dimensional one-component plasma
entries.abstract: The two-dimensional one-component plasma is a system of point charges that repel each other logarithmically, in a uniform neutralizing background. When the inverse temperature $β$ is at most $2$, we prove that its correlations decay exponentially, and that its Gibbs state is unique among point processes whose fluctuations are controlled. This constitutes part of the fluid phase predicted by physicists. As a consequence, we obtain the existence of an infinite-volume limit, extending the Ginibre point process, which we call $\mathrm{Gin}_β$. We show that its truncated two-point function, at the scale of the Debye length, is given to first order in $β$ by the Debye-Hückel approximation.

entries.title: Time-changed Compound Poisson Process
entries.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a time-changed compound Poisson process (TCCPP) obtained by subordinating the classical compound Poisson process (CPP) with a subordinator and an inverse subordinator, which are defined via distinct Bernstein functions. We study the governing equations and distributional properties of a TCCPP including its moments, dependence structure and limiting behaviour. We derive distributions of the integrated CPP and a linear combination of TCCPPs. We also obtain the law of iterated logarithm, the central limit theorem and weighted sum representation for a TCCPP. Finally, we provide some characterizations of a TCCPP in terms of martingales, a univariate multinomial process, a triangular array process and waiting time distribution. The proposed framework generalizes several existing fractional stochastic processes and offers greater flexibility for modelling complex count data.

entries.title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
entries.abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.

entries.title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
entries.abstract: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

entries.title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
entries.abstract: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

entries.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
entries.abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

entries.title: Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process
entries.abstract: We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.

entries.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
entries.abstract: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$. Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-Émery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

entries.title: Sitewise Generator Decomposition and Non-Equilibrium Steady States for Generalized Zero-Range Processes
entries.abstract: In this paper we study the generalized zero-range processes considered in [20, 11, 12] with boundary driving. In these processes mass is moved between neighboring sites with rates depending only on the departure site. For a wide class of such models, the equilibrium stationary states are known to be of product form. We show that for such models, the boundary-driven generator can be decomposed into a sum of generators acting on single sites when integrating against (possibly inhomogeneous) products of the equilibrium marginals. We exploit this structure to derive new results for the harmonic models introduced in [15]. In particular, we prove that the propagation of mixture measures in [19] is still valid on graphs with asymmetric edges. On the chain geometry with asymmetric edges, we identify a class of models for which the NESS is given precisely by the NESS of the symmetric harmonic model on the chain. In addition to these results for harmonic models, we also present a new class of asymmetric models on the chain for which the NESS can be found explicitly and exhibits shock behavior. The large deviations for the density profile corresponding to these NESS are stated and proved.

entries.title: Spectral distribution for biased orientations of random graphs
entries.abstract: We study the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind for biased orientations of Erdos-Renyi random graphs. In the model $D(n,p,p')$, an edge is present with probability $p$ and, conditional on its presence, is directed from its smaller to its larger endpoint with probability $p'$. Both parameters may depend on $n$, and biased tournaments are the special case $D(n,1,p')$. We prove a global semicircle law whenever $n(p(1-p)+3p^2p'(1-p')) \to \infty$, for both the centered and the uncentered matrix, and also for the expected empirical spectral measure. Our second theorem gives the exact spectrum of the mean matrix and the limits of the extreme eigenvalues on the scale $np$, under a sufficient density assumption. The main difference from the unbiased random orientations (where $p'=1/2$) is emergence of multiple large eigenvalues. The proofs include the closed-walk counting, control of the moment variances, an explicit diagonalization of the deterministic bias, and the passage from centered to uncentered spectral measures.

entries.title: A Proof of the Achlioptas-Friedgut Convergence Conjecture
entries.abstract: For every fixed integer $q\ge3$, we show that the $q$-colourability transition in a sparse random graph takes place at a limiting edge density, thus proving the Achlioptas-Friedgut convergence conjecture. The proof adapts the argument we recently introduced to settle the satisfiability conjecture.

entries.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
entries.abstract: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

entries.title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
entries.abstract: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.

entries.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
entries.abstract: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios

entries.title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
entries.abstract: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

entries.title: The probability that a branching random walk does not hit a point
entries.abstract: We study the probability that a branching random walk in ${\bf Z}^d$ driven by a Galton-Watson tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices does not hit a fixed point. For $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this probability behaves like $n^{-α/4}$ in logarithmic scale, where $α=4$ when $d=1$, $α=2\sqrt{2}$ when $d=2$, and $α=(\sqrt{17}-1)/2$ when $d=3$.

entries.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
entries.abstract: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<α<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^α$ at small times to order $t^{2α}$ at large times.

entries.title: Percolation on grandparent graphs of Bienaymé trees
entries.abstract: We consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the grandparent graph of a Bienaymé tree, obtained by adding to the tree an edge between every vertex and its grandparent. We show that the critical parameter $p_c$ is the unique solution of an explicit equation involving the generating function of the offspring distribution, and we study how $p_c$ depends on this distribution beyond its mean $m$. When $m\geq 1.569$, the offspring distribution concentrated on the (one or two) integers closest to $m$ is the unique maximiser of $p_c$ among all offspring distributions with mean $m$, and its critical parameter is $\frac1{m^2}-\frac1{m^3}+O\left(\frac1{m^4}\right)$ as $m\to\infty$; more generally, for two distributions that are comparable in the convex order, $p_c$ is larger for the smaller of the two distributions under the condition that its support bounded some explicit $N(m)$ of order $m^4$. These restrictions cannot be removed: the convex order alone does not determine the order of the critical parameters, even among distributions with support bounded by $O(m^4)$, and the extremal property fails for $m$ close to $1$. Finally, for every $m>1$, the critical parameter $p_c$ can be arbitrarily close to $0$ for general offspring distributions with mean $m$. If we only consider offspring distributions that do not charge $0$, so that the obtained tree is almost surely infinite, this remains true if and only if $m\geq 2$.

entries.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
entries.abstract: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $η^{-2(d+1+α)}\leδ\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(μ^N-u_η)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_η$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $η$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_iΘ_i}dW_i)$, with $Θ_i=σ_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $δ$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.

entries.title: Laguerre tessellations in spaces of constant curvature and their sectional distributions
entries.abstract: We determine the sectional distributions of Poisson--Laguerre tessellations in spaces of non-zero constant curvature, proving closure under totally geodesic sections and deriving explicit weight intensity measures. This includes sections of Poisson--Voronoi tessellations. We construct the generalised polar region, a new geometric object which extends existing polar constructions for both positive and negative curvature and provides an alternative representation of Laguerre tessellations. We also give deterministic conditions for tessellation existence and establish sharp integrability criteria for Poisson--Laguerre tessellations.

entries.title: Mass gap for the fractional $Φ^4_2$ model
entries.abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $Φ^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Boué-Dupuis variational formula.

entries.title: The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of erdős problem 521
entries.abstract: We resolve Erdős Problem~521 by proving that the normalized real-root count $N_n/\log n$ of Rademacher polynomials almost surely has no limit. More generally, consider the Kac polynomials \[ P_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}ξ_jx^j \] with i.i.d.\ real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment. Let $N_n$ denote the number of distinct real roots of $P_n$. We prove that, almost surely, \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{N_n}{\log n}=\frac1π+C_*, \] and the set of subsequential limits is exactly \[ \left[\frac1π,\;\frac1π+C_*\right]. \] Here $C_*>1/π$ is a constant uniquely determined by an equation. The lower-limit identity remains valid under the weaker assumption that $\mathbb{E}|ξ_0|^{2+δ}<\infty$ for some $δ>0$.

entries.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
entries.abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

entries.title: Niche construction as an emerging phenomenon from fast ecological and slow evolutionary-environmental timescales in individual-based models
entries.abstract: We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. In this setting, extinction and/or emergence of entities with negligible size or rarity, on long time scales can be observed. We prove that the joint dynamics of the environment and the species sizes on a logarithmic scale undergo a piecewise deterministic Markov process in a large time regime, which can be approximated by an explicit dynamical system in the limit of large populations. This convergence result holds true under the assumption that no "bad event" occurs during the population dynamics, corresponding to situations where several species become dominant or go extinct simultaneously. We also prove that no such bad event occurs for Baire-almost all initial conditions of the population sizes and the environmental resources. We apply this framework to study the long term coexistence of two specialist species consuming two resources, with a "joint" niche construction where each species constructs the niche of the other while depleting its resources. We also study an example of immune escape in cancer, where the environmental variable is associated with the state of the immune system and the species are associated with three types of tumor cells.

entries.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
entries.abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

entries.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
entries.abstract: We provide an efficient implementation of combinatorial Bernoulli factories. Such a factory turns coins of unknown biases $x$ into a random vertex of a polytope $P$ whose mean is exactly $x$. For every affine slice of the cube (the class of polytopes that admit a factory), we give a single algorithm whose expected number of coin flips and running time at every interior $x$ are polynomial in the dimension and in $1/{δ_*}$, where ${δ_*}=\min_i\{x_i,1-x_i\}$ is never supplied to the algorithm. For perfect matchings this gives $O(n^{8}{δ_*}^{-2}\log(n/{δ_*}))$ flips, while the factory of Niazadeh, Paes Leme, and Schneider [STOC 2021] spends at least $n^{2n-1}$ flips in expectation at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix. For other polytopes, our method rounds exactly given a point deep inside $P$ and the promise that $x$ is far from the boundary of $P$.

entries.title: Radius decay and boundary polymers: cluster expansion for long-range many-body tilts
entries.abstract: We consider a nearest-neighbor Gibbs measure on a region in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (e.g., the Ising model) tilted by $\sum_{x,r} g_{x,r}$, where $g_{x,r}$ is an arbitrary function of the spins in the ball of radius $r$ about $x$, with $\|g_{x,r}\|_\infty\leq \exp(-C r)$: an exponential decay in the radius of the ball rather than in its volume. Standard cluster expansions fail for such many-body tilts, as a ball of radius $r$ carries $\exp(c r^2)$ configurations. We show that the partition function can be resummed into a polymer model whose polymers are outer boundaries of connected unions of balls, decorated by the spins along them, with weights decaying exponentially in the boundary length. The proof uses only the domain Markov property of the base measure; it develops a version of this resummation argument that appeared in a recent work of the authors in the context of RG analysis of Grassmann variables. As applications, we show convergent cluster expansions for many-body tilts of Ising models at high and low temperatures; existence of infinite-volume limits; and exponential decay of correlations.

entries.title: Signature representations of certain BSDEs
entries.abstract: We link the solvability of backward stochastic differential equations with time-augmented Brownian signature data to the solvability of a differential equation on the tensor algebra of signature coefficients. We show that in certain cases the solutions are of closed form and remain within the class of linear functionals of the signature. Lastly, we derive a closed-form solution to a pricing and hedging problem in terms of the time-augmented Brownian signature.

entries.title: Universal sampling rules for the signed friendship paradox
entries.abstract: The friendship paradox describes a bias in mean degree induced by neighbour sampling. We study signed weighted networks, with transitions proportional to edge magnitudes and signed strength as the vertex score. We characterize all positive initial weights, depending on total strength and score, that guarantee a nonnegative one-step mean change on every connected graph. Without regularity assumptions, the same condition yields stochastic dominance at every fixed time. Continuous admissible rules are precisely total strength multiplied by a positive continuous nonincreasing function of the score. It is enough to test connected graphs with at most five vertices and two vertex types. The bound of five is optimal even for continuous rules; the proof uses a sharp four-vertex energy inequality. The complete score vector alone cannot determine a universally valid initial law with full support. Under marked local convergence and suitable integrability assumptions, we also obtain joint limits for local conditional mean score increments and compute an explicit limiting law and mean for independently signed random regular graphs. Under joint cut-norm convergence of the magnitude and signed kernels and uniformly bounded normalized strengths, we also obtain Wasserstein convergence of the sampling-weighted distributions of normalized local biases and convergence of their means.

entries.title: A posteriori error estimates for fully coupled McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with jumps
entries.abstract: We prove a two-sided a posteriori error estimate for numerical approximations of fully coupled McKean-Vlasov forward-backward SDEs with jumps under full-tuple law dependence. The coefficients may depend on the joint law of $(X,Y,Z,U)$, and we allow infinite jump activity. We construct a computable estimator ${\mathcal{E}_π}$ for the squared full-tuple error ${\mathcal{D}_π}$ relative to the exact Euler solution. The estimator uses the boundary and cumulative residuals of any admissible grid approximation. Under monotonicity and on sufficiently fine grids, $c\,{\mathcal{E}_π} \le {\mathcal{D}_π} \le C\,{\mathcal{E}_π}$. The efficiency bound holds without monotonicity or a mesh restriction. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the continuous-time error up to a discretisation remainder that vanishes under coefficient time regularity. Closed-form and state-nonlinear benchmarks cover full-tuple law dependence, mark-dependent jump integrands, nonzero orthogonal martingales and infinite jump activity. In our experiments, the estimator tracks the discrete error during neural training and across Picard iterations. In a mean-field inventory model, we use the estimator and a computable discretisation term to bound the excess cost of the computed control over the discrete optimum.

entries.title: Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
entries.abstract: The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.

entries.title: Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions
entries.abstract: We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions. Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.

entries.title: Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails
entries.abstract: We study non-Hermitian matrices $Y_n$ obtained by normalizing each row of an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. entries to Euclidean norm one. We consider regularly varying radial tails of index $α\in[0,2]$, with $α=0$ denoting slowly varying tails, and the broader normal domain of attraction. For $0<α<2$, assuming angular tail convergence, we prove convergence in probability of the empirical singular value measures of every shift $Y_n-zI$ to deterministic laws characterized by the root resolvent of a column-normalized directed Poisson weighted infinite tree, extending the framework of Bordenave, Caputo and Chafai (arXiv:1006.1713). Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $μ_α^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $δ_0$ as $α\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $α\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<α\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.

entries.title: How shared pedigrees shape gene genealogies in finite admixed populations
entries.abstract: Gene genealogies along a chromosome are dependent not only because nearby alleles tend to experience no recombination and are therefore inherited together, but also because alleles at different loci may share parental histories through a common ancestor. Disentangling physical linkage and shared parental trajectories is key to understanding how demography shapes genetic diversity. We develop a mathematical framework for describing the joint genealogies of sampled alleles in a finite admixed population, tracing their ancestry backward to the source populations while explicitly accounting for parental relationships and recombination events. Under a Wright--Fisher model, we show that the joint gene genealogy forms an absorbing Markov chain, derive the likelihood of local ancestry, and connect it to other quantities of interest, notably the admixture fraction. We further establish that, once demographic parameters become constant, local ancestry converges to distinct limiting distributions depending on the demographic setting. Under isolation, chromosomes undergo infinitely many recombination events and linkage disequilibrium is due to drift within population replicates, retaining traces of past admixture events. Under constant gene flow from source populations, recent contributions progressively erase the influence of earlier ancestry. Using the joint genealogy of two alleles, we obtain the limiting variance of admixture fractions in both regimes. We illustrate our framework's flexibility through simulations of endogamy and selection. These examples show how genetic diversity depends on the structure of underlying parental relationships. Our work provides a framework for specifying and analyzing complex demographic scenarios and clarifies the links between local ancestry and mating patterns.

entries.title: Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web
entries.abstract: The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $Λ_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(Λ_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $Ω_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $Ω_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $Ω_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$. In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $Ω_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $Ω_N^\infty$.

entries.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
entries.abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

entries.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
entries.abstract: We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem. We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.

entries.title: Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion
entries.abstract: We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.

entries.title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
entries.abstract: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $β>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $θ_1,θ_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.

entries.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

entries.title: An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model
entries.abstract: We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.

entries.title: Exact Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Conditional Empirical Measures of Killed Diffusion Processes
entries.abstract: Let $M$ be a $d$-dimensional compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ with boundary $\pp M$, and let $X_t$ be the diffusion process generated by $L:=\DD+\nn V$ for some $V\in C^2(M)$ which is killed on the boundary. For any initial distribution $ν$ which is not fully supported on $\pp M$, let $μ_t^ν$ be the conditional empirical measure for the diffusion process under the condition that the process is not yet killed at time $t$, and let $μ_0$ be the associated quasi-stationary distribution. We derive the sharp convergence rate of $μ_t^ν$ to $μ_0$ in the quadratic Wasserstein distance $\W_2$ as $t\to\infty$. In particular, if $ν(B(x,r))\asymp r^k$ for some $k\in [0,d]$ and all $r\in [0,1]$ uniformly in $x\in {\rm supp}ν$, then for large $t>0$ $$ \W_2(μ_t^ν,μ_0)\asymp_ν\begin{cases} t^{-1},&d-k<6,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t},&d-k=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d-k+2}{2(d-k-2)}},&d-k>6. \end{cases} $$ Moreover, letting $\rr_\pp(x)$ be the distance of $x$ to $\pp M$, for large $t>0$ we have $$ \W_2(μ_t^{\dd_x},μ_0)\asymp \begin{cases} t^{-1},&d\le 3,\\ t^{-1}\log (1+\rr_\pp(x)^{-1}), & d=4,\\ t^{-1} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1}, & d=5,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1},&d=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d+2}{2(d-2)}}\rr_\pp(x)^{-\ff 4{d-2}},&d\ge 7. \end{cases} $$

entries.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
entries.abstract: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.

entries.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
entries.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.

entries.title: Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$
entries.abstract: We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $Σ_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+σ^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $Σ_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehatΣ_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehatΣ_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $χ^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $χ^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.

entries.title: The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees
entries.abstract: We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.

entries.title: Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks
entries.abstract: Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.

entries.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule
entries.abstract: Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)Π$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(μ+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.

entries.title: Gaussian processes with random pointwise regularity
entries.abstract: Using wavelet series, we construct Gaussian stochastic processes whose pointwise Hölder exponent is random along a typical sample path, although at every fixed point the exponent is deterministic almost surely. We first give a local non-sparsity condition under which the Hölder exponent almost surely is a deterministic function. In the opposite direction, a lacunary construction shows that the exceptional set on which the exponent is modified can have full Hausdorff dimension. For this model we determine the marginal multifractal spectra and the bivariate spectrum of the deterministic series and its Gaussian randomization.

entries.title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
entries.abstract: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(α^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $α\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.

entries.title: Polarity of the First Dirichlet Liouville Spectral Gap
entries.abstract: We prove zero $1$-capacity of first-gap collisions for the minimal Liouville spectral Green-response form and its canonical extension. The minimal-form diffusion avoids collisions for every initial law absolutely continuous with respect to the spectral law.

entries.title: On the continuity of martingale optimal transport in higher dimensions
entries.abstract: We investigate qualitative and quantitative continuity of martingale optimal transport under perturbations of both marginals in dimensions $d\geq2$. We assume that each pair of marginals admits a reference martingale coupling whose density relative to the product of its marginals is bounded above and away from zero, uniformly along the sequence. If the limiting target measure is not carried by a hyperplane, we prove continuity under $W_1$-convergence for continuous costs of at most linear growth, assuming only finite first moments. For Lipschitz costs, a uniform $p$-moment bound on the targets, $p>1$, yields an explicit stability estimate with exponent $(1-1/p)/2$; uniformly bounded target supports give exponent $1/2$. The proof constructs a correction of couplings with small martingale bias while preserving both marginals. Truncated moment corrections allow the target measure to have unbounded support. The construction also shows that every martingale coupling of the limiting marginals can be approximated in $W_1$ by martingale couplings of the approximating marginals. We also discuss counterexamples showing that neither the uniform density condition nor non-degeneracy of the limiting target measure can be omitted in general.

entries.title: Strong Well-Posedness and Path-by-Path Uniqueness for Fractional SDEs with Integrable Drifts
entries.abstract: In dimension $d$, we consider stochastic differential equations driven by additive fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H<1/2$ and with a time-dependent drift that is $p$-integrable in space and $q$-integrable in time. Under the subcriticality condition $\frac{Hd}{p}+\frac1q<1-H$, complemented by two integrability conditions needed for Girsanov's theorem, we prove strong existence and path-by-path uniqueness of solutions. We also establish stability with respect to the initial data and the drift, both pathwise and in moment norms, and construct a Hölder continuous semiflow. When $H$ approaches $1/2$, our conditions reduce, up to an endpoint case, to the condition of Krylov and Röckner (2005) for Brownian motion, and in dimension one they complement the results of Nualart and Ouknine (2003), which rely on comparison arguments. Our methods combine the stochastic sewing lemma, Lyons' rough path theory, and the quantitative John--Nirenberg inequality for stochastic processes of vanishing mean oscillation.

entries.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
entries.abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

entries.title: Sharp Bounds for Near-Maximizers of Gaussian Processes
entries.abstract: For a centered Gaussian process $G$ with continuous sample paths on a compact metric space $T$, a continuous drift $f: T \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, a noise level $σ>0$, and $ε\ge 0$, let $A_ε$ be the set of points at which $f+σG$ is within $ε$ of its maximum. Writing $\mathbb{E}\sup_TG$ for the expected supremum of $G$, we prove that the expected squared diameter of $A_ε$ in the canonical pseudometric of $G$ is at most $8ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$ and that the expected maximal squared distance from a point of $A_ε$ to an exact maximizer is at most $4ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$. The constants cannot be improved uniformly over index sets, processes, and drifts, and no logarithmic factor in $ε$ appears, unlike in bounds integrated from tail estimates. At $ε=0$ the bounds give the almost sure uniqueness of the maximizer in the canonical pseudometric without nondegeneracy assumptions. Given this uniqueness, both bounds follow from a bound with constant $2$ on the mean square of the largest increment of an independent copy of $G$ from an exact maximizer to a point of $A_ε$. The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $ε$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.

entries.title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
entries.abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities.
