On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$. In $d\ge5$, when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to $C(p/N+\sqrt p M^{-d})$. For fixed $p$, the sharp order is $N^{-1}+M^{-d}$ on star-containing windows and $N^{-1}$ on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.

entries.title: Continuum hierarchical Cannings process: I. Construction, duality and dichotomy
entries.abstract: We construct spatial measure-valued Cannings processes on the \emph{continuum} hierarchical group $Ω_N^\infty$ of order $N\in\N$ (an uncountable topological group with an ultrametric distance). These processes arise as the continuum-space limit of spatial Cannings processes on the \emph{discrete} hierarchical group $Ω_N$ of order $N\in\N$ (a countable topological group with an ultrametric distance) analysed in \cite{GHKK14}. On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

entries.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
entries.abstract: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

entries.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
entries.abstract: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

entries.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

entries.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
entries.abstract: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-Mélou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

entries.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
entries.abstract: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $μ_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.

entries.title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
entries.abstract: We study properties of optimal trajectories for the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs in general GJN.

entries.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
entries.abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

entries.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
entries.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

entries.title: Permutons
entries.abstract: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

entries.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
entries.abstract: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincaré inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

entries.title: Khintchine's limit theorem for monotone convolutions
entries.abstract: We prove that every weak limit of monotone convolution powers is monotonically infinitely divisible. In contrast, we prove that every probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ can occur as a weak limit of monotone convolutions of an infinitesimal triangular array. We also discuss similar limit theorems for multiplicative monotone convolution on the unit circle.

entries.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
entries.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

entries.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
entries.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

entries.title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
entries.abstract: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.

entries.title: Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers
entries.abstract: We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/ω$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.

entries.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
entries.abstract: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ generated by configurations $Γ$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies Hölder regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.

entries.title: Triadic and assortative structure of absorbing states in the Axelrod model
entries.abstract: We study the Axelrod model of cultural dissemination, viewed as a finite-state Markov chain on an arbitrary finite graph, and classify its absorbing states. An absorbing configuration splits the edges into interior edges, whose endpoints share their whole culture, and boundary edges, whose endpoints share nothing. A partition of the vertices into connected blocks is the domain partition of some absorbing configuration exactly when its quotient graph is properly $q$-colourable. The configurations with a given domain partition correspond to homomorphisms from the quotient into the $F$-fold categorical power of $K_q$, so their total number is a sum of chromatic polynomials over connected partitions; this gives closed forms for trees and cycles and the value $2^{n+F-1}$ for $q=2$ on connected graphs. In absorbing configurations no triangle carries exactly one boundary edge, the open-wedge mass of the interior graph is at most that of the host graph, and Newman's assortativity coefficients for domains, cultures and single features are ordered. The feature counts are martingales and their sums of squares submartingales, which yields an absorption-time bound of order $n^2$ that is attained on paths. Exhaustive enumeration and simulations illustrate the results.

entries.title: Stationary causal enhancements of fractional Brownian motion at small Hurst indices
entries.abstract: We construct stationary, complete-past causal geometric enhancements of prescribed multidimensional fractional Brownian motion for every $0<H\leq1/4$. They retain the first level, are exactly self-similar, and commute with linear coordinate maps. The construction removes a remote-past cutoff from Volterra signatures. At reciprocal indices $H=1/N$, a lagged top-degree logarithmic-velocity subtraction yields a quantitative joint cutoff and zero-lag limit with sharp moment bounds. Centered velocities and white-noise localization provide the critical cancellation. The limit is stable under weak concentration at zero of deterministic mass-one signed lag profiles on a common bounded lag range, with uniformly bounded total variation. Top-central perturbations give nonuniqueness at nonreciprocal indices, preserving all lower levels and symmetries. At reciprocal indices, square-integrable whole-line causal extensions with fixed lower levels and common-noise shift and scaling identities differ by a deterministic central drift. Logarithmic centering removes this drift. The enhancements yield controlled integration, rough differential equations, a finite-word regularity-structure model and an adapted realization by ordinary signatures.

entries.title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
entries.abstract: These notes (which grew out of some lecture notes prepared for the first Aarhus Summer School in Analysis and Probability) are an introduction to the parabolic Anderson model (PAM), or otherwise stated the stochastic heat equation $\partial_{t} u \,=\, \tfrac{1}{2}Δ\, u \,+\, β\, u\,\dot{W}$. In this system, a multiplicative random potential $\dot{W}$ drives the solution away from the smooth spreading of the classical heat flow and toward intermittency. Namely one observes that mass concentrates, as time grows, on a few tall and widely separated peaks. Through the Feynman-Kac representation this analytic phenomenon has an equivalent probabilistic reading as the localization of a directed polymer in a random environment. We first develop this picture on the flat space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, covering the construction of the driving noise, well-posedness of the equation, and two-sided bounds on the moment Lyapunov exponents that quantify intermittency. We then turn to the more original goal of the monograph: understanding how these phenomena, and the exponents attached to them, change when $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is replaced by a genuinely geometric background, such as a sub-Riemannian manifold or a fractal set. Throughout, the emphasis is on concepts, main results, and the intuition behind their proofs, rather than on exhaustive technical detail.

entries.title: Fourth-Moment Theorems for Sums of Multiple Wigner Integrals
entries.abstract: We derive quantitative free fourth-moment bounds for sums of two Wigner chaoses of opposite parity under mirror symmetry. The bound contains an explicit remainder consisting of internal contractions of the two kernels. In particular, vanishing of this remainder together with the fourth free cumulant implies convergence to the standard semicircular law. If the higher-order kernel is cyclically symmetric, the internal contractions can be moved to an endpoint and we obtain an explicit fourth-root bound without a remainder. For fully symmetric kernels we obtain a square-root bound under the $W_2$-Wasserstein distance. Using the operator-norm support estimate for Wigner integrals, we also extend these bounds to every $W_p$-Wasserstein distance , where $1\le p<\infty$.

entries.title: Rate of convergence for the Wiener--Itô chaos in $W_p$ for $1\leq p<\infty$
entries.abstract: Inspired by previous work of Nualart, Ledoux, Peccati, Nourdin, and others, we establish quantitative fourth moment theorems for random variables in a fixed Wiener--Itô chaos and for sums of two Wiener--Itô chaoses in the $W_p$-Wasserstein distance for $1\leq p<\infty$.

entries.title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
entries.abstract: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.

entries.title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
entries.abstract: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.

entries.title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
entries.abstract: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

entries.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
entries.abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

entries.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
entries.abstract: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $α$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $α$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $α_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Matérn-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.

entries.title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
entries.abstract: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

entries.title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
entries.abstract: Bar-Lev and Letac (2025) introduced the concept of chainability of infinitely divisible distributions on $\mathbb R$. In this note, we show that a simpler notion of chainability can be used for infinitely divisible distributions on $[0,\infty)$. We derive some properties and give a probabilistic interpretation in terms of so-called size-biased distributions. As an application, we discuss simulation from size-biased distributions associated with an important class of tempered stable distributions.

entries.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
entries.abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

entries.title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
entries.abstract: We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.

entries.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
entries.abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

entries.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
entries.abstract: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

entries.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
entries.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $θ(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{θ(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

entries.title: Martingale representations without finite or well-defined mean
entries.abstract: The classical Strassen theorem characterizes convex order through martingale representations under the assumption of finite first moments. We show that a natural reformulation of the theorem remains true on the real line for distributions without finite or even well-defined means. We further investigate the higher-dimensional setting, where this equivalence fails in general. Martingale representations are nonetheless guaranteed in higher dimensions when every nonzero linear projection of the second marginal has undefined mean.

entries.title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics
entries.abstract: We develop a variational and geometric theory based on statistical physics for the joint evolution of Transformer attention and token representations at fixed model parameters. To this end, we introduce a free energy for the attention and model the evolution of the attention weights by its Fisher--Rao gradient flow. At fixed token representations, we prove that the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimiser and that every positive attention trajectory converges to it. For prescribed time-dependent representations, we show that the attention dynamics becomes linear after a change to logit variables. This result yields tracking bounds relative to the instantaneous softmax and sufficient conditions for attention to converge to a fixed matrix. Hamiltonian dynamics for the representations and their momenta are then coupled to the attention relaxation driven by the same energy. This coupling results in an energy-dissipation law. We also develop two alternative Hamiltonians incorporating the attention value map. We prove global well-posedness of the attention flow and all three coupled systems.

entries.title: Iteration-Clock Selection for Euler Schemes of Degenerate Diffusions
entries.abstract: We study Euler--Maruyama approximation of the driftless one-dimensional SDE $dX_t=σ(X_t)\,dW_t$ when $σ$ vanishes at the origin and weak uniqueness fails because solutions may remain at zero for an arbitrary time. The central object is the logarithmic coefficient profile $q(Q)=-\logσ(e^{-Q})$. Under a two-sided logarithmic increment condition, with both indices in $(0,1/2)$, we show that weak-solution selection is governed by a deterministic iteration clock: if $N_q(Q)$ is the number of iterates of $q$ needed to reach a fixed reference depth and $hN_q(\log(1/|x_h|))\to d$, then the Euler scheme started from $x_h$ converges to the fundamental zero-sojourn diffusion delayed by $d$. This single theorem yields the common-index generalized-power law $d=θ/|\logα|$ when $h\log\log(1/|x_h|)\toθ$, an effective translation-number formula for periodically modulated logarithmic profiles, a two-index delay window, and a sharpness construction in which, for one coefficient and one initialization family, the cluster set is the entire delay window. Thus the macroscopic selection mechanism is the iteration count of the logarithmic coefficient profile; the explicit double-logarithmic law of the homogeneous power case is its common-index closed form.

entries.title: Remarks on spectral gaps on Gaussian path space
entries.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the relationship between spectral gaps of Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/$L^2$ operators on Gaussian path space and the underlying Volterra kernel $F$. This framework includes fractional Brownian motion $B^H$ with Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. For the fractional Wiener measure $μ_H$, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with respect to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Dirichlet form holds for $H\geq\frac12$, whereas the corresponding weak Poincaré inequality fails for $0<H<\frac12$. The damped/$L^2$ Dirichlet forms satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for every $H\in(0,1)$.

entries.title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schrödinger operators
entries.abstract: For a subordinated Schrödinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schrödinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schrödinger operator.

entries.title: Strong relaxed dynamics in stochastic control
entries.abstract: We characterize relaxed dynamics for which any finite family of strong state solutions, together with their relaxed inputs, can be approximated by the prescribed controlled dynamics, ground-stably in law. Relaxed inputs include parametrizations of relaxed controls over the unit interval. Unlike relaxed controls, these parametrizations determine action couplings. The proposed relaxed dynamics is driven by a single cylindrical Brownian motion in a Hilbert space. For each relaxed input, its state is the unique strong solution of the corresponding equation. The collection of these states, over all relaxed inputs, satisfies the approximation requirement. Conversely, suppose one assigns to each relaxed input a continuous adapted state process on a fixed probability space. Pairwise approximation forces the assignment to be the strong solution map of the same dynamics, for a unique cylindrical Brownian driver. In fact, even for a state map indexed by (non-parametrized) relaxed controls, the relevant relaxed control class admits coherent parametrizations under separability and finite-family approximation assumptions, and the same type of dynamics is recovered again.

entries.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
entries.abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.

entries.title: Removing the floor from Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for finite-population U-statistics
entries.abstract: Let $C$ be a uniformly sampled $n$-element subset of a finite population $D$ of size $N$, and let $U_C$ be the complete U-statistic of order $k$ built from a bounded kernel on the $k$-subsets of $D$. We prove a product inequality for the uniform distribution on $\binom{D}{n}$ and deduce from it the comparison $ \log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{θ(U_C-\mathbb{E}U_C)}\right] \le \frac{n}{k}\log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{kθ}{n}(Y-\mathbb{E}Y)}\right]$, where $Y$ is a single kernel value taken at a uniformly sampled $k$-subset of $D$. This yields Hoeffding, Bennett and Bernstein inequalities for $U_C$ with effective sample size $n/k$ in place of the $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ available so far. The gain is negligible when $n$ is much larger than $k$, but it approaches a factor of two in the exponent when $k$ is close to $n$.

entries.title: Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables II
entries.abstract: In this paper, based on the concept of step-weighted distribution, we introduce a minimum-deformation approach to constructing comonotonic and moment-matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables. The proposed approach aims to minimize the Pearson deformation of a starting comonotonic approximation subject to moment-matching constraints. We establish several results concerning the existence and uniqueness of minimum-deformation comonotonic approximations and propose a method for determining the step quantiles and weights. In particular, when the number of steps is one greater than the moment-matching order, we show that the joint optimization problem can be reduced to an optimization problem involving only the partition points. The proposed framework accommodates moment matching of any prescribed finite order, and numerical experiments demonstrate its application to approximations matching the first five moments of the original sum. The numerical results also show that minimizing the Pearson deformation does not necessarily improve the approximation accuracy of risk measures, which depends on both the starting comonotonic approximation and the choice of partition points and correction weights.

entries.title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
entries.abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $η>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(η^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

entries.title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
entries.abstract: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $α$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $α> 1/2$ and for the case $α=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

entries.title: A Geometric Construction of the Radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam Processes
entries.abstract: We provide a geometric construction of the radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam processes for arbitrary root systems and arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicity parameters. This is a broad class of processes including the classical Bessel process, Dyson Brownian motion, and the Dyson Bessel process. We find that, when $x_t$ is a certain anisotropic Markov diffusion process in a symmetric space $G/K$ or its tangent space at the origin, invariant under an appropriate $K$-action, the evolution in the space of orbits can be described as a radial Dunkl or Heckman-Opdam process (respective to whether the diffusion is on the tangent space or $G/K$ itself). These processes can have arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicities, analogous to arbitrary values of $β$ in Dyson Brownian motion. In a freezing limit, analogous to $β\to \infty$ for Dyson Brownian motion, these processes become motion by mean curvature of the orbits. A connection to finite free probability is also discussed, in which we provide a geometric interpretation of certain properties related to finite free position.

entries.title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
entries.abstract: We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $ϕ^\star(α)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula. Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre $z$ equals $\barW(z)\,\Up$, where $\barW$ is the degree function of the graphon and $\Up=-(\Id-P)^{-1}[P(H_ρρ)]'$ is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with $m$ edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of $z$. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.

entries.title: The satisfiability conjecture for random k-SAT formulas. Human-friendly exposition of the recent OpenAI resolution
entries.abstract: The satisfiability conjecture was one of the most important open problems in discrete probability. It was resolved recently first by Carenini~\cite{GCarenini}, and shortly after by OpenAI~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}, among other 370 problems solved by its internal model. The conjecture concerned the satisfiability property of random instances of the k-SAT problem. It posits the existence of a fixed value for the clause-to-variables ratio around which the probability that the formula is satisfiable drops sharply from nearly one to nearly zero as the ratio increases. While the case of large constant $k$ was resolved a decade ago by Ding, Sly and Sun~\cite{ding2015proof,ding2022proof} using the heavy machinery of the second moment method, the case of general $k$ eluded proof until ~\cite{GCarenini} and~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}. In this short note we provide a ''human-friendly'' and detailed exposition of the OpenAI's resolution of the conjecture.

entries.title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
entries.abstract: In this paper, we provide a new set of tools for establishing the number rigidity of point processes which are particularly well suited for the spectral processes of stochastic operators. These tools allow one to prove the number rigidity of a wide class of stochastic operators that had been previously inaccessible to the standard methods in the area, such as the variance of linear statistics, which require being able to precisely analyze correlations between individual points. We propose an alternative mechanism which uses a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of the unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise which allows one to convert the probabilistic problem into a more tractable perturbation theory problem. This new approach allows us to prove the rigidity of previously inaccessible operators including those with heavy tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. As a demonstration, we use these tools to prove the number rigidity of new classes of stochastic Schrödinger and Sturm-Liouville Operators which are resistant to analysis using the standard rigidity toolkit.

entries.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
entries.abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.

entries.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
entries.abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

entries.title: Extreme-value asymptotics for smallest enclosing balls of spherically symmetric samples
entries.abstract: Let $R_n$ denote the radius of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ sample of spherically symmetric random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $D_n$ be the sample diameter. While the asymptotic behaviour of $D_n$ is well understood, much less is known about $R_n$. Starting from a classical result of Daniels for planar Gaussian samples, we develop a point-process approach to the asymptotic behaviour of $R_n$ in the three classical extreme-value regimes. We obtain limit theorems in the Gumbel, Fr'echet and Weibull cases, with the limiting laws described by geometric functionals of Poisson point processes. In dimension two, the Gumbel limit can be identified explicitly and is universal within the corresponding max-domain of attraction. We also study the asymptotic relationship between $R_n$ and $D_n$ and the supporting configurations of the smallest enclosing ball.

entries.title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq α\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.

entries.title: Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincaré Inequalities on Graphs
entries.abstract: We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincaré inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincaré inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{π/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al. Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.

entries.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
entries.abstract: We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.

entries.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
entries.abstract: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.

entries.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
entries.abstract: We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$. Finally, we extend our results to fractional and integrated Brownian sheets.

entries.title: Backward--forward interacting systems with probability-valued strategies and common noise
entries.abstract: We study a system of interacting agents in which a backward stochastic equation is coupled to the forward evolution of a probability-valued strategy distribution. The agents interact through their empirical state--strategy law and are exposed to a common Brownian noise. Under Lipschitz, mass-conservation, and positivity assumptions, we establish well-posedness of the finite-agent system on a sufficiently short time interval. We then identify its large-population limit as a conditional mean-field backward--forward system and prove conditional propagation of chaos. When agent characteristics take finitely many values, we obtain order $N^{-1}$ bounds for the expected squared particle--copy error and the expected squared Wasserstein distance of order one between the empirical law and the conditional limiting law. An adaptive-strategy model with replicator dynamics illustrates the theory, accompanied by a numerical comparison of the two errors.

entries.title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
entries.abstract: We determine sharp universality thresholds for quotients of the free profinite group $\widehat F_n$ on $n$ generators by $n+u$ independent random relations, where $u$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. For products of mutually independent uniformly coset-balanced factors, convergence to the Liu--Wood measure $μ_u$ holds when the minimum number of factors grows faster than $\log n$, which is a uniformly sharp condition. For random words of fixed length $\ell_n$, convergence holds exactly when $\ell_n$ is eventually odd and $\ell_n-\log n\to\infty$. We also prove universality for randomly ordered products of independent integer powers under the balance condition $nα_{n,p}/\log n\to\infty$ at each fixed prime, recovering finite-prime cokernel laws by abelianization.

entries.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
entries.abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,δ_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\leδ_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $δ_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $ρu\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+ρ^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $ρ^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $δ_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/ρ$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-Černý complexity function as $d\to\infty$.

entries.title: An INAR(1) Risk Model with by-claims applied to the PFAS issue
entries.abstract: We propose there a new type of unidimensional discrete-time risk model in ruin theory involving both main claims and by-claims, where the latter ones are counted thanks to an INAR(1) process. In this way, the model embodies a contagion phenomenon, which may be used to describe the damages caused and covered by an insurance company ensuing the spreading of PFAS compounds in the environment. We present mostly asymptotic ruin probabilities, and multiple comparisons with other models derived from the aforementioned one, in particular with two models where the dependence assumptions are relaxed.

entries.title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
entries.abstract: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\llη\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.

entries.title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
entries.abstract: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.

entries.title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
entries.abstract: On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators. Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.

entries.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
entries.abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

entries.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
entries.abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.

entries.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
entries.abstract: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

entries.title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
entries.abstract: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

entries.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
entries.abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $μ$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

entries.title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
entries.abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.

entries.title: Positivity Improving Quantum Markov Operators
entries.abstract: A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.

entries.title: A tractable transition function for the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection via gamma duality
entries.abstract: The transition function of the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection is a fundamental object for non-neutral evolutionary modelling and likelihood-based inference, but, unlike in the neutral case, existing representations are impractical or inefficient. Spectral approaches rely on truncation levels that grow with selection strength and the number of alleles, thus leading to rapidly increasing computational costs, while existing duality-based expansions lead to multi-type dual processes whose transition probabilities involve intractable normalising constants. In this paper we obtain a new transition-function representation for the multi-allelic Wright-Fisher diffusion with parent-independent mutation and genic selection that makes transition-law evaluation and simulation practically feasible in regimes where existing methods are costly or unavailable. The key tool is a new gamma duality, obtained by augmenting classical polynomial duality by an exponential tilting and yields a multivariate birth-death dual with fully explicit infinitesimal rates and an entrance-boundary construction. This is used to express the Wright-Fisher transition law as an explicit mixture of standard Dirichlet components, with mixing weights obtained from the dual started from its entrance boundary. We characterise the dual stationary distribution and its small-time behaviour, and develop practical and efficient sampling procedures for both transition and stationary laws, including a fast approximate stationary sampler with explicit error control. Numerical experiments illustrate substantial runtime gains over specialised methods in regimes where they apply, while our approach remains applicable for arbitrary numbers of alleles and selection coefficients.

entries.title: Interacting Urn Schemes on Infinite Graphs: A Representation Approach
entries.abstract: Interacting urn schemes have emerged as an important framework for studying reinforcement phenomena in interacting stochastic systems (see, e.g., \cite{launay2011interacting,launay2012generalized,WARM2014,aletti2017interacting,Synchronisation-2,kaur2023interacting,kaur2023interacting2}). Most existing results, however, are restricted to finite systems. In this article, we investigate interacting urn schemes involving infinitely many urns, where the interactions are naturally described by a directed graph. The reinforcement or drawing mechanism at each urn depends on the compositions of its in-neighboring urns. To analyze the asymptotic behavior of these systems, we develop a representation of the urn dynamics in terms of branching Markov processes evolving on a class of random forests introduced in this article. This extends the representation approach of \cite{bandyopadhyay2022new}, originally developed for single Pólya urn schemes, to interacting urn schemes on locally finite directed graphs. Using this representation, we establish almost sure convergence of the color proportions under standard conditions on the reinforcement matrix or kernel. In particular, we show that the convergence holds independently of the topology of the underlying graph, and hence our results also apply to undirected graphs, where the interactions are bidirectional. We further investigate measure-valued generalizations and other related reinforced stochastic processes, illustrating the broad applicability of the representation approach. Finally, we discuss connections with self-organized criticality.

entries.title: Weak and strong discretization errors for signatures of Gaussian processes
entries.abstract: Let $X$ be a continuous Gaussian process in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, with independent components of roughness $H\in(\tfrac14,1)$, possibly with a linear drift, and let $X^n$ be its piecewise-linear interpolant on a mesh of width $δ$. We study how well the truncated signature of $X^n$ approximates that of the natural lift of $X$, in mean (the weak error) and in $L^2$ (the strong error). Over a class of drivers defined by quantitative regularity conditions, the weak error at every fixed truncation level is $O(δ^{γ(H)})$ with $γ(H)=\min(2H,4H-1)$, uniformly over the class, and for truncation levels $M\ge4$ fractional Brownian motion attains this rate. For centred drivers the weak error vanishes at levels $1$ to $3$, Gaussian or not. It first appears at level~$4$, where we compute its leading constant for independent fractional Brownian motion in $d=2$: on $(\tfrac12,1)$ it is $1/(2\sqrt3)$, independent of $H$, and on $(\tfrac14,\tfrac12)$ it is given by a $ζ$-series. For fractional Brownian motion with drift, a level-$3$ error of the same order appears for $H\ge\tfrac12$. Below $\tfrac12$ the drift reaches the rate only at levels $\ge5$ (proved for $d\ge3$). The strong error is of exact order $δ^{2H-1/2}$ for fractional Brownian motion with $H\in(\tfrac12,1)$, so in mean square the weak error lies a full power of $δ$ below it. For $H\le\tfrac12$ the strong error is $O(δ^{\vartheta})$ for every $\vartheta<2H-\tfrac12$, uniformly over the class, and the exponent $2H-\tfrac12$ cannot be improved. Finally, we construct pairs of laws in the class whose mesh data have the same law but whose expected signatures differ by order $δ^{γ(H)}$. Hence no quantity computed from the mesh data has mean within $o(δ^{γ(H)})$ of the expected signature uniformly over the class.
